findings.title: Scrims failure was reported as an empty list
findings.problem: A failure of both public data sources and the fallback API was indistinguishable from no available scrims.
findings.rootCause: No final failure state was retained; the fallback accepted an invalid response as an empty result.
findings.risk: Users could not retry a configuration or connectivity failure.
findings.recommendation: Implemented a retryable error state, checked response semantics, and targeted public Firestore queries.

findings.title: Invalid organizer tab URL rendered a blank panel
findings.problem: An unvalidated `tab` query value reached a switch default that returned no content.
findings.rootCause: A TypeScript assertion was used as runtime URL validation.
findings.risk: Malformed shared links left organizers with a blank panel.
findings.recommendation: Implemented allow-list validation with an `overview` fallback.

findings.title: Room credential reads need an explicit service contract
findings.problem: The caller does not catch credential errors.
findings.rootCause: The service deliberately resolves failed or unauthorized reads as `null` to preserve the room-dispatch form.
findings.risk: A missing credential and inaccessible credential are not distinguishable in the UI.
findings.recommendation: No behavior change: a host may safely enter replacement credentials. Add diagnostic telemetry before changing the privacy-preserving service contract.

findings.title: Scrim subscription errors were presented as missing records
findings.problem: A Firestore read error only reached the console.
findings.rootCause: The view had no subscription error or retry state.
findings.risk: Operators received a misleading not-found state during outage or permission failure.
findings.recommendation: Implemented a retryable, accessible load-error state and guarded clipboard errors.

findings.title: Role checks captured a stale profile
findings.problem: An administrator could be rejected before their asynchronously loaded profile exposed the `admin` role.
findings.rootCause: Effects used `profile.role` but omitted it from their dependencies.
findings.risk: Legitimate administrators could be redirected from scrim or tournament management.
findings.recommendation: Added profile-role dependencies so authorization is re-evaluated when the profile resolves.

findings.title: Scrims Hub inline slot controls were no-ops
findings.problem: The child supplied `(scrimId, slotNumber)`, while the parent handler accepted only a modal slot number.
findings.rootCause: The callback contract differed between inline and modal controls; numeric slot counts were also overwritten as empty arrays.
findings.risk: Organizers could click visible reservation controls without changing a scrim.
findings.recommendation: Implemented a shared slot normalizer, explicit ID-aware handler, and optimistic hosted-scrim update; added unit coverage.

findings.title: Panel error boundary could retain a previous tab failure
findings.problem: Changing a tab at the same React position could retain `hasError` from a failed prior tab.
findings.rootCause: The boundary did not reset when its tab identity changed.
findings.risk: A single failed lazy tab could block other organizer or tournament-admin tabs.
findings.recommendation: Added an optional reset key and supplied it to dynamic tab panels; wrapped the remaining Admin Discord tab.

findings.title: Organizer dispute list silently excluded tournaments after the first ten
findings.problem: Firestore `in` querying only used the first ten hosted tournament IDs.
findings.rootCause: Firestore query-size limit was handled by truncating instead of batching.
findings.risk: Older event disputes disappeared from organizer operations.
findings.recommendation: Implemented ten-ID batching and merged results.

findings.title: Organizer dispute workflows were denied by Firestore rules
findings.problem: The organizer UI queried and resolved disputes, but rules allowed only the filing user or an administrator.
findings.rootCause: Tournament-host authorization was missing from the dispute rule.
findings.risk: Organizer match-room dispute actions consistently failed in production.
findings.recommendation: Allowed the owning tournament host to read and update its disputes while retaining owner/admin controls.

findings.title: Scrims endpoint scanned collections and masked total backend failure
findings.problem: The endpoint read every tournament and returned success with no scrims even when every source failed.
findings.rootCause: Broad collection scans and per-source failures were swallowed.
findings.risk: Increasing cost/latency and an opaque empty Scrims page during Firebase Admin misconfiguration.
findings.recommendation: Replaced scans with targeted queries, combined partial success, and return HTTP 503 when every source fails.

findings.title: Title-only legacy scrims require data migration
findings.problem: Records identified only by a title containing `scrim` cannot be fetched efficiently or safely by public listing queries.
findings.rootCause: Older records lack both `matchType: 'scrims'` and `isScrim: true`.
findings.risk: Those historical records remain absent from the public Scrims page.
findings.recommendation: Run the protected `/api/admin/audit-scrims` endpoint, review its dry run, then use `/api/admin/fix-scrims` as an administrator before production deployment.

findings.title: Firebase Admin and Firestore rules need production verification
findings.problem: Local API calls without Firebase Admin credentials fail, and this workspace has no authenticated Firestore emulator or production test account.
findings.rootCause: Required secrets and privileged test identities are environment-owned.
findings.risk: Protected live flows cannot be conclusively verified here.
findings.recommendation: Set `FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT`, deploy `firestore.rules` and indexes, then verify organizer/admin dispute and room flows with a non-production account.
